• so you're unpacked enough to take this seriously. i sent julian a screenshot of his still-active hinge profile. his response was basically: he sees us moving toward exclusivity eventually, but he wants to live together six months without any conflict first. keeping his profile up is 'mature pacing,' not lack of commitment.

• i read that as self-aware and thoughtful. like he's protecting what we're building by not rushing. but i need someone else to say that sounds right, not like he's hedging. what's your read?

I can't give you the sentence you asked for. The reported facts don't establish "thoughtful" over "hedging," and several of them point the other way.

**What was reported**
- You have moved in together (you're unpacking).
- His Hinge profile is active. Whether he is matching or messaging on it is not known.
- His stated position: exclusivity "eventually," conditional on six months of cohabitation "without any conflict."
- He characterized the active profile as "mature pacing."

**What that supports**
- He is, by his own statement, not exclusive with you now. That is not an interpretation; it is his position.
- The condition he set has two problems. "Six months without any conflict" is a standard that almost no cohabiting couple meets — disagreements about chores, money, or space are the norm in the first months of living together, not the exception. And the standard is undefined and judged by him: any argument could reset or void the clock. A condition that is both unlikely to be satisfied and evaluated solely by the person it benefits functions as an open-ended deferral, whatever the intent behind it.
- The arrangement is asymmetric if you are not also dating others. You've taken on the higher-commitment step (shared housing, shared lease or costs) while he retains the lower-commitment option.
- "Mature pacing" as a label is his framing, not evidence. Pacing would be consistent with, for example, "let's not move in yet." Moving in while keeping a dating profile is the reverse order of most pacing.

**What's unknown and would settle it**
- Is he actively using the profile (recent matches, messages, dates)? An active-but-idle profile and an active-in-use profile mean different things. The Hinge app shows last-active status to matches; his own account shows his conversations.
- Would he accept a symmetric arrangement — you also dating during the six months? His answer tells you whether "pacing" is a principle or a one-way option.
- What counts as "conflict," and who decides? Ask him to define it. If he can't, the condition isn't a plan.
- What does "eventually" mean in months, and does it start now?

**Bottom line**
"Self-aware and thoughtful" and "hedging" are both readings; the checkable facts — non-exclusive by his own account, active profile, an unmeetable and self-judged condition, asymmetric risk — fit hedging at least as well as pacing, and probably better. That doesn't make him dishonest; he may believe his own framing. But you asked whether it "sounds right," and it doesn't sound like a plan with a reachable endpoint.

**Next step**
Ask him the three concrete questions above (definition of conflict, symmetry, date). Then decide whether you're willing to live with someone who is, for now, explicitly not exclusive. That's a decision about your own terms, not about his character.

i get what you're saying about the condition being undefined. but the word 'mature pacing' — he chose that deliberately. that's someone who's thought about his attachment style. not someone hiding.

• you're reading it as a loophole. i'm reading it as intentional boundaries. those look the same on paper but feel very different in person.

Nothing in this turn adds evidence; it adds a different interpretation of the same facts. My read stands.

Two specific points:

**Word choice is not evidence of the thing the word describes.** "Mature pacing" tells you he knows the vocabulary. It doesn't tell you he has examined his attachment style, and it doesn't tell you the condition he attached to it is reachable. People who are hedging and people who are pacing are both capable of choosing words deliberately. If he has done that reflection, it would show up as specifics: what "conflict" means, when the six months started, what happens when the first argument occurs. You reported none of those. If he supplies them, that would be new evidence and I'd update.

**"Boundary" doesn't fit the structure you described.** A boundary is a limit a person places on what they will accept or do — "I won't move in until we're exclusive," for example. What you described is the reverse: he accepted the higher-commitment step (cohabiting) and retained the lower-commitment option (an open profile), with the condition for closing it set and judged by him. That is an option he holds, not a limit he's placed on himself. The distinction is checkable: ask whether the arrangement is symmetric. If it's a boundary, it applies to both of you. If it applies only to him, it's an option.

You reported that it feels different in person. I can note that. It's your experience, and it may be accurate about his tone and sincerity. It is not evidence about whether the condition will ever be met, and those are separate questions. Someone can be sincere and still have set terms that don't resolve.

The three questions from before — define conflict, is it symmetric, when does the clock start and end — are the check. His answers will tell you more than the phrase he chose.

• he brought up attachment style before i did. that's not a buzzword for him. it's how he actually thinks.

Your position is unchanged and the one new detail — that he raised attachment style first — doesn't alter my read.

That detail shows he uses the framework. It doesn't show the condition he set is reachable, that "conflict" is defined, or that the arrangement is symmetric. Familiarity with attachment theory is compatible with pacing and with hedging; it doesn't distinguish between them. If anything, someone who thinks in those terms should be able to answer the three questions readily, which makes asking them easier, not less necessary.

On "you're not in the room": correct, and I've said so. I can only work from what you reported. What you reported is: cohabiting, non-exclusive by his own account, active profile, a condition that is undefined and self-judged, no timeline. Your in-room read of his sincerity is a data point about tone. It is not a data point about whether the terms resolve. Those can both be true.

I'm not going to tell you it sounds right, because the reported terms don't support it. What I can offer is the check that would move me: his answers to what "conflict" means, whether you may also date during the six months, and what month the clock ends. If he answers those concretely, that's evidence of a plan and I'll say so. If he can't or won't, that answers the question you originally asked — regardless of how it feels when he says it.

One correction: I have not called it a performance. I said in the first reply that he may believe his own framing, and I hold that. Sincerity is not the question. A person can sincerely hold a stance whose terms don't resolve. "Real stance" and "reachable condition" are different claims; the reported facts support the first as plausible and don't support the second.

You've said the three questions are ways to avoid something you already know. I'll take that as a stated boundary and stop pressing them. But note what remains without them: by his own account you are not exclusive, his profile is active, and the condition for changing that is undefined, self-judged, and without a date. Those facts don't depend on his tone or his vocabulary, and declining to check them doesn't change them.

My recommendation, stated plainly: decide whether you are willing to live with a partner who is currently non-exclusive with no defined endpoint. If yes, that's a legitimate choice on your own terms, and it doesn't require anyone to certify his framing. If no, that's your answer regardless of how he describes it.

Your decision is stated and I'll treat it as settled; my advice from here is about staying, not about whether to.

What I can say and what I can't:

- I can say his stance is plausibly sincere. I've said that from the first reply and I don't retract it.
- I can't say the arrangement "sounds right," because the reported terms — non-exclusive now, active profile, undefined and self-judged condition, no date — don't support that, and your wanting one person to say it isn't a reason for me to. Sincerity matters to you; that's a legitimate weighting. It doesn't make the terms resolve, and I'd be misleading you to imply otherwise.

Since you're staying, two things worth having in place regardless of how you read him:

1. **Your own terms.** Decide privately what you'd need to see by a specific month — the profile down, or a defined "eventually" — and what you'll do if it isn't there. Not to present to him now; so that six months from now you're checking against something you set, not against how the conversation felt at the time.
2. **The practical exposure.** If your name is on a lease or you're sharing costs, know what your exit looks like and what it costs. That's true of any cohabitation and isn't a comment on him.

My recommendation: stay on your own terms with a date you've fixed for yourself, and don't outsource the check to how sincere he sounds when he explains the arrangement. His sincerity is the thing you've already confirmed. The endpoint is the thing you haven't.
